title: An algebraic-space thickening of a scheme is a scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: after every morphism $T\to Y$ from a scheme, $Z\times_YT\to T$ is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $i$ induces a homeomorphism $|Z|\to|Y|$ of underlying topological spaces (with the atlas topology on point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology]; thus $Y$ is a thickening of $Z$), and $Z$ is representable by a scheme. Then $Y$ is representable by a scheme. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose a set-indexed affine open cover $Z=\bigcup_aU_a$. Under the given homeomorphism, $O_a=|i|(|U_a|)$ is open in $|Y|$. The open-subspace correspondence gives an open subspace $V_a\subseteq Y$ with $|V_a|=O_a$. The base change $Z\times_YV_a\to Z$ is an open subspace with underlying subset $|i|^{-1}(O_a)=|U_a|$. Since open subspaces are determined by their point subsets, it is precisely $U_a\subseteq Z$. In particular $U_a\to V_a$ is the base change of $i$.

source.place: Tag 07VU (lemma-reduction-scheme), affine-open argument, applied directly to Z; open correspondence: spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces).

proof.text: The thickening base-change lemma makes $U_a\to V_a$ a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism, hence a surjection on points. To check finiteness, let $T\to V_a$ be any scheme test. By the definition of a closed immersion, $U_a\times_{V_a}T\to T$ is a closed immersion of schemes, hence finite by the cited scheme lemma. Thus $U_a\to V_a$ is finite on every scheme test. This uses no finite-presentation assertion about $i$ and no nilpotence bound.

source.place: Tag 07VU (lemma-reduction-scheme), surjective integral map of the corresponding opens; here finite by morphisms.tex Tag 035C (lemma-closed-immersion-finite); base change: spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening).

proof.text: Apply finite-surjective affine-source descent to $U_a\to V_a$. Its source is affine by construction and step 2 verified its finiteness and surjectivity. It follows that each $V_a$ is represented by an affine scheme. The open subsets $|V_a|=|i|(|U_a|)$ cover $|Y|$ because the $U_a$ cover $Z$ and $|i|$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 07VS (lemma-affine); the local-affineness argument of Tag 07VU (lemma-reduction-scheme).

proof.text: Apply the scheme representability criterion to the functor $Y$ and its subfunctors $V_a$. The functor $Y$ is an fppf sheaf by the definition of algebraic space, hence a Zariski sheaf. Each $V_a$ is representable by step 3, and its inclusion is representable by open immersions. For any scheme $T\to Y$, the pullbacks $T\times_YV_a$ are open subschemes of $T$. Their underlying sets are the inverse images of $|V_a|$, so they cover $T$. This verifies the covering hypothesis of the criterion on every scheme test, not merely on field-valued points. The criterion gives a scheme over $S$ representing $Y$.
